theater: 底格里斯河東岸阿舒爾

battle.name: 阿舒爾的陷落
battle.theater: 底格里斯河東岸阿舒爾
battle.brief: 前614年，米底王基阿克薩雷斯與巴比倫王那波帕拉沙聯軍攻破亞述聖城阿舒爾。約兩米長、槍尾帶銅套的斯巴達長矛屬希臘重步兵的傳統，近東同時期只見於希臘與卡里亞傭兵之手；真正決定城破的是複合弓、騎兵與圍城工程，而不是成建制的長矛方陣。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 聯軍一方是巴比倫王國與米底王國。巴比倫王那波帕拉沙於前626年自立為王，在加爾底亞南部徵發步兵與弓箭手，王室直轄的常備兵與城邦民兵混合編組，攻城所需的大型器械由國家的工匠與工匠村供給。米底一方是王基阿克薩雷斯於前625年驅逐西徐亞人後整編的軍隊：他把原先按親族分幫、各人只使自己擅長武器的部落民團，改成由國家統一配發裝備、分為戰略與戰術單位的常備軍。兩軍合圍時，由巴比倫人負責封鎖河道、修築營壘與操控攻城器械，米底人提供主力突擊兵與繞側的騎兵。亞述一方是崩解中的帝國殘軍：國王辛沙里什昆把大部分可用兵團留在尼尼微，阿舒爾城內只剩城防軍、王室侍從與從各省抽調來的附屬部隊，其中也包括早年在亞述軍中服役過的希臘與卡里亞傭兵。兩邊的指揮都極度集中：聯軍由兩王共節制，亞述則因帝國崩解而分裂成互不支援的守軍。
countriesEn: The besieging side was a coalition of Babylonia and Media. The Babylonian king Nabopolassar had crowned himself in 626 BC, drawing infantry and archers out of Chaldea in the south; his royal standing troops were mixed with civic militia, and the great siege machines were supplied by state craftsmen and by the artisan settlements. The Median side was the army rebuilt by king Cyaxares after he overthrew Scythian rule in 625 BC: he replaced the old kin-banded tribal levies, in which every warrior used whichever weapon he handled best, with a regular army fully equipped by the state and organised into strategic and tactical units. Once the two armies closed on the city, the Babylonians took charge of sealing the river, building the camps and working the siege engines, while the Medes supplied the main assault troops and the cavalry that worked around the flanks. The Assyrian side was the rump of a collapsing empire: king Sinsharishkun kept most of the usable army at Nineveh, so the city of Assur held only its garrison, the royal retinue and detachments drawn from the provinces, among them Greek and Carian mercenaries who had served in Assyrian armies in earlier reigns. Command on both sides was sharply concentrated: the coalition was directed jointly by the two kings, while Assyria, once the empire began to break up, was split into garrisons that could not support one another.
people: 決定攻城節奏的是兩位國王。巴比倫王那波帕拉沙是迦爾底亞王朝的開國者，前626年在巴比倫自立，隨後把戰爭推進到亞述腹地，他不需要一個站得住的正統名號，只需要能養得起軍隊與工匠的稅基。米底王基阿克薩雷斯是這場戰爭中真正贏得戰場的人：據希羅多德記載，前627年他在底格里斯河畔擊潰亞述王辛沙里什昆的軍隊；他上位的第二年便把部落民團改造成編制軍，兵員與裝備由國家供給，這是聯軍能長期圍城的前提。狄奧多羅斯稱他「阿斯蒂巴拉」，意譯「持矛者」，其子阿斯提阿格斯的名字意譯「擲矛者」，米底王室的姓名本身就以矛為榮。亞述方面的關鍵人物是末代國王辛沙里什昆，他選擇死守尼尼微而任由阿舒爾被圍，兩個決定互相矛盾，最後兩地都失守。至於阿舒爾城頭的指揮者，現存編年史沒有留下名字，只留下城破時血肉模糊的記錄。
peopleEn: Two kings set the pace of the siege. Nabopolassar of Babylon, founder of the Chaldean dynasty, crowned himself in 626 BC and then carried the war into the Assyrian heartland; he needed no defensible claim to a legitimate title, only a tax base able to pay for soldiers and craftsmen. Cyaxares of Media was the man who actually won the field: according to Herodotus he destroyed the army of the Assyrian king Sinsharishkun on the banks of the Tigris in 627 BC, and in the second year of his reign he turned tribal levies into a regular army whose men and equipment were supplied by the state, the precondition for a siege that could be sustained. Diodorus Siculus calls him Astibaras, rendered as spear bearer, and his son Astyages carries a name meaning spear thrower; the Median royal house advertised the spear in its own names. The decisive figure on the Assyrian side was the last Assyrian king, Sinsharishkun, who chose to hold Nineveh and left Assur to be surrounded; the two decisions contradicted each other and in the end both cities were lost. No name survives for the commander on the walls of Assur: the chronicles record only the carnage of the breach.
kits: 這件兩米長、槍尾帶銅套的斯巴達長矛，是這張卡的兵器，年代定在前800年前後，屬於希臘重步兵的裝備。誠如卡上所說，它在方陣裡比劍更早決定誰站得住——希臘人靠它把站得穩變成一種制度。放進這場戰爭看，阿舒爾城頭並沒有成建制的希臘方陣：長矛近戰在美索不達米亞向來讓位給弓箭，這一點在希羅多德記錄的前627年底格里斯河戰役裡已經寫得很清楚，亞述人手中只有弓而無矛，戰敗者因此全軍失去反擊之力。米底與巴比倫的攻城主力同樣以弓為骨，接近城牆的短兵相接則靠長柄矛、劍與盾。真正被記錄下來的攻城器材是攻城塔、撞槌、壕溝與土壘，以及把軍隊與糧食運過底格里斯河的羊皮筏和驢隊。阿舒爾城牆上部署的是亞述式的複合弓手，鎧甲以鐵片與鱗甲為主；與此同時，在同一時期的兩河傭兵市場上，希臘與卡里亞傭兵攜帶長矛與青銅圓盾為兩河諸王效力，這正是這件長矛在近東的落腳點——它不是攻城的主兵器，而是同一時代新步兵制度的標誌。至於阿舒爾城頭究竟有沒有這種長矛手的編制，現存記錄並無可核的明細，只能確定近東的圍城兵器體系裡並沒有它的一席之地。
kitsEn: This two-metre wooden spear with a bronze socket at its butt end is the weapon on the card, dated to around 800 BC and belonging to the equipment of the Greek heavy infantry. As the card says, in the phalanx it decided who could still stand long before the sword did: the Greeks turned standing your ground into a system. Set inside this war, there was no Greek phalanx drawn up on the walls of Assur. Close combat with the spear had always given way to the bow in Mesopotamia, and Herodotus makes the point plainly for the battle on the Tigris in 627 BC: the Assyrians had bows but no spears, and the defeated army lost its means of reply altogether. The besieging Median and Babylonian armies were likewise built on the bow, with long-handled spears, swords and shields for the fighting at the foot of the walls. The siege equipment actually recorded consists of siege towers, battering rams, ditches and earthen embankments, together with the skins and mule trains used to move troops and grain across the Tigris. On the walls of Assur the defenders were Assyrian composite bowmen in armour of iron plate and scale. At the same time, in the mercenary markets of the two rivers of that age, Greek and Carian mercenaries carried long spears and bronze round shields in the service of the kings of Mesopotamia; that was where this spear found its footing in the Near East. It was never the main siege weapon, but the emblem of a new infantry doctrine forming in the same generation. As for whether any formation of such spearmen stood on the walls of Assur, no record allows the detail; what is certain is that the weapon had no place in the Near Eastern siege inventory.
tactics: 這是一場典型的圍城與破城戰。聯軍先在去年取下阿拉帕，作為前進的跳板；到阿舒爾城下，分割包圍，於底格里斯河兩岸築壘掘壕，切斷城內與南方盟友的聯繫，同時封鎖河面，不讓糧食與援軍從水上進入。圍城方需要時間：壕溝、土壘、攻城塔與撞槌都要人推、要有木料、要有糧，而亞述人在城頭用弓壓制，不讓工程部隊貼近。攻城軍在缺口處的攻勢是短兵相接——後來在城址發現的成堆骸骨，說明城破之後仍有巷戰式的肉搏，雙方在土城與殘垣之間用刀、矛、斧近身廝殺。聯軍內部的配合是巴比倫人管工程與封鎖、米底人管衝鋒與騎兵繞側，攻城最要命的一擊是突然而不是猛烈。亞述方的弱點不在城牆，而在指揮：尼尼微的兵團不能來援，遠方行省的守軍各自為戰，援兵被分割後逐個被吃掉；城內糧食靠運入的份額有限，圍得越久，弓手的體力與箭矢存量越低。而聯軍的騎兵在城外始終控制著周邊道路，決定了援軍與糧車的生死。
tacticsEn: This was a siege and a breach, fought in the classic manner. The coalition had taken Arrapha the year before as a stepping stone for the advance; at Assur they surrounded the city on several sides, dug in and threw up earthworks on both banks of the Tigris, cut the city's links with its allies to the south, and closed the river so that no grain and no reinforcement could come in by water. The besiegers needed time: ditches, embankments, towers and rams all had to be pushed forward by men, needed timber and needed rations, while the Assyrians on the walls kept up bow fire to stop the engineers from coming close. The assault at the breach was hand to hand. The heaps of skeletons later found at the site show that bloody fighting continued after the city fell, with men cutting one another down among rubble and broken walls with swords, spears and axes. Inside the coalition the division of labour ran along lines of capability: the Babylonians handled engineering and blockade, the Medes the assault and the flanking cavalry, and the killing stroke depended on surprise rather than on weight. The weakness of the Assyrians lay not in their walls but in their command. The army at Nineveh could not come to the rescue, provincial garrisons fought their own separate battles, and relief columns were cut up and destroyed one by one. Rations inside the city depended on what could be carried in, and the longer the siege ran the weaker the bowmen became and the fewer arrows they had. Outside, coalition cavalry held the roads throughout, and that was what decided the life or death of every relief column and grain convoy.
data: 可核的數字不多，先寫確定的：前615年聯軍取下阿拉帕，前614年圍攻並攻下阿舒爾，前612年尼尼微淪陷，前609年哈蘭陷落，亞述帝國就此終結。阿舒爾是前26世紀建立起來的城市，到陷落時已延續約三千二百年，是世界上少數有連續斷代的古城之一。城址連同辛那森那胡在底格里斯河上架牆包住的市郊，考古估算占地約四百公頃量級；城牆以土坯砌成，高處達數十米，牆面立有塔樓。亞述帝國全盛時的疆域自埃及尼羅河延伸到印度河流域，是當時已知最大的帝國。戰役本身的精確兵力數字沒有留下來：編年史只說圍城方能自巴比倫與米底持續調來軍隊與器械，守方只剩殘部。可以引的旁證有兩條：希羅多德記載前627年底格里斯河一役屍體塞河，河水為之不流；考古在阿舒爾城址的井渠與街巷中出土大量人骨，其中不少帶有兵器傷痕，與破城後血肉橫飛的記述相合。
dataEn: The verifiable numbers are few, so take the certain ones first. The coalition took Arrapha in 615 BC, besieged and captured Assur in 614 BC, Nineveh fell in 612 BC, and Harran fell in 609 BC, at which point the Assyrian Empire was finished. Assur had been founded in the 26th century BC, so by its fall it had run for roughly three thousand two hundred years, making it one of the few cities anywhere with an unbroken archaeological record. The site, together with the suburbs that Sennacherib walled across the Tigris, is estimated by archaeologists to cover something on the order of four hundred hectares; the walls were built of mud brick, rose to several tens of metres at their highest, and carried towers along their length. At its height the Assyrian Empire reached from the Nile in Egypt to the Indus, and was the largest empire then known. No exact troop figures for the siege itself survive: the chronicles say only that the besiegers could keep bringing up men and machines from Babylonia and Media, while the defenders were reduced to a rump. Two pieces of corroborating evidence can be cited. Herodotus records that after the battle on the Tigris in 627 BC the river was choked with the dead and its current was checked. And the excavations at Assur have brought up large numbers of human bones from the wells, channels and street levels of the city, many bearing weapon wounds, consistent with the account of a city taken by slaughter.
cause: 打起來的原因不是一場決戰，而是帝國晚年同時壞掉的幾件事。前631年亞述巴尼拔死後，王位繼承引發內戰，他的兩個兒子先後即位又先後被殺，宮廷與行省的忠誠一起鬆掉；安納托利亞、高加索、黎凡特與巴比倫的起義此起彼伏，帝國的稅基與徵兵管道同時收縮。前626年巴比倫在南方脫離亞述，那波帕拉沙以加爾底亞的力量建國，其軍隊與亞述同城卻不同語族，仇恨最深；前625年米底王基阿克薩雷斯用一場宴席除掉西徐亞人，結束了外族在米底高原的統治，再照亞述與烏拉爾圖的樣子把散兵編成軍隊——亞述教會他怎麼打仗，他拿來打亞述。前627年他在底格里斯河畔擊敗辛沙里什昆的野戰大軍，切斷了亞述最後一次主動出兵的機會。此後雙方都知道，亞述的問題不是輸一場，而是再輸一次就沒有第二個帝國。
causeEn: The war did not begin with a single decisive battle; it began with several things failing at once in the late empire. When Ashurbanipal died in 631 BC, the succession broke into civil war: his two sons came to the throne and were killed in turn, and the loyalty of the court and the provinces loosened together. Revolts in Anatolia, the Caucasus, the Levant and Babylonia followed one another, and the empire's tax base and recruitment channels shrank at the same time. In 626 BC Babylonia in the south broke away from Assyria, and Nabopolassar founded a state on Chaldean strength; his people shared Assyria's cities but spoke another tongue, and their hatred ran deepest. In 625 BC Cyaxares of Media killed the Scythians at a banquet, ended the foreign yoke over the Median highlands, and then drilled his scattered warriors into an army on the Assyrian and Urartian model: Assyria had taught him how to wage war, and he turned that lesson against Assyria. In 627 BC he destroyed the field army of Sinsharishkun on the banks of the Tigris, removing the last chance for Assyria to take the initiative. From then on both sides understood that Assyria's problem was not losing a battle but losing once more and having no second empire behind it.
impact: 阿舒爾陷落的直接後果是亞述的國家機器被連根拆掉。亞述的國名、祭司系統與文字傳統原以這座城市為中心，聯軍破城之後，埃沙拉神廟與伊什塔爾神廟被劫掠焚毀，國王的象徵連同城牆一起倒塌；那波帕拉沙在巴比倫立起勝利石碑，把亞述的主神刻成提著籃子與鐵鍬、俯首被踐踏的囚徒，宣告新王朝自居為亞述的正統繼承者。遠期看，這場戰爭決定了東地中海與近東的權力版圖：亞述的先例被新巴比倫帝國全盤接收，後來同一支軍隊會走向耶路撒冷；米底人則成為東方強國，與巴比倫既合作又提防，最終在亞述廢墟上再打一場。對希臘世界來說，阿舒爾的消息同時帶來兩重刺激：一方面，希臘城邦在同一個世紀裡靠重步兵方陣與長矛建立起自己的霸權，看見近東靠圍城與騎兵仍能傾覆帝國；另一方面，希臘人從此把北方的蠻族一律稱作亞述人或敘利亞人，把對方的焚城與屠殺記成野蠻的標準，阿舒爾的殘垣因此成為後世最長久的一個反面教材。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the fall of Assur was that the Assyrian state machine was torn out at the root. The name Assyria, the priestly system and the written tradition of the realm had all been centred on this city; after the breach, the Esharra temple and the temple of Ishtar were plundered and burned, and the symbols of the king came down with the walls. Nabopolassar set up his victory stele in Babylon, carving the Assyrian chief god as a captive holding a basket and a spade, bowed and trodden underfoot, and thereby announced the new dynasty as the legitimate successor of Assyria. In the long run this war fixed the balance of power in the eastern Mediterranean and the Near East. The Assyrian precedent was taken over wholesale by the Neo-Babylonian Empire, and the same armies would one day march to Jerusalem; the Medes rose as a great eastern power, allied to Babylon yet watchful of it, and would eventually fight a second time over the ruins of Assyria. For the Greek world the news of Assur carried a double stimulus. On one side, the Greek poleis were building their own hegemony in the same century with phalanxes of heavy infantry and long spears, and they could see that the Near East had brought down an empire by siegecraft and cavalry. On the other, the Greeks now called all the northern barbarians Assyrians or Syrians, and fixed the burning of cities and the killing of their populations as the standard of savagery, so that the ruins of Assur became the longest-lived negative example in their literature.
result: 城破之後，聯軍在阿舒爾城內大肆劫掠，把神像、金屬、器物與糧食一併搬走，再縱火焚燒主要街區與宮廟；現存的編年史記載破城時有慘烈的近身肉搏，考古在城址發現的大量骸骨與之呼應。阿舒爾此後再未被亞述人重建，城市被擄走的居民分批安置在巴比倫與其附屬地，亞述聖城的神廟在巴比倫統治下勉強維持了二十餘年，後於前590年米底人反叛時被毀。亞述王權退到哈蘭，由一位亞述人將軍自立為王，前609年哈蘭也淪陷，帝國正式終結；前605年那波帕拉沙死後，其子尼布甲尼撒二世接手這個已經改寫了東方的王國。那波帕拉沙在巴比倫神廟豎立的勝利石碑，連同阿舒爾城址下層數千年的堆積，成為這一場戰爭留下的兩件硬證：石上是一個王朝的自陳，坑裡是一個王朝的終點。
resultEn: After the city fell, the coalition plundered Assur without restraint, carrying off the divine statues, the metal, the vessels and the grain, and then set fire to the main quarters and the palace. The surviving chronicles describe savage hand-to-hand fighting at the breach, and the great quantity of bone found at the site bears that out. The Assyrians never rebuilt Assur. The inhabitants who were carried off were settled in Babylon and its dependencies, and the temples of the Assyrian holy city limped on for more than twenty years under Babylonian rule before they were destroyed when the Medes revolted in 590 BC. The Assyrian kingship withdrew to Harran, where an Assyrian general crowned himself king, and Harran too fell in 609 BC, ending the empire for good. When Nabopolassar died in 605 BC, his son Nebuchadnezzar II inherited a kingdom that had already remade the east. The victory stele that Nabopolassar set up in a temple of Babylon, together with the thousands of years of strata beneath the site of Assur, are the two hard pieces of evidence this war left behind: on the stone, a dynasty's account of itself; in the pit, the end of a dynasty.
